source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:5 (the Masorah)
claim_en: THE ONE PATACH FATHER: 'every אב (father) in all Scripture is pointed qamatz — except ONE with PATACH: כי אב המון גוים' (17:5). The single differently-voweled father-word in the Bible sits INSIDE THE RENAMING SENTENCE — the אב of av-hamon ('father of a multitude') that turns Avram into Avraham. SNAPSHOT: patach, exactly there.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:6 (the Masorah: 'none like it')
claim_en: THE FRUITFUL-VERB SPLIT, lean side: והפרתי ('and I will make you fruitful' — to ABRAHAM) — defective, and the Masorah marks it UNIQUE. SNAPSHOT: the only defective token of the word in the Torah.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:6 (the Masorah's 'two plene')
claim_en: THE FRUITFUL-VERB SPLIT, full side: the word's two PLENE tokens are Ishmael's blessing ('as for Ishmael, I have heard you — והפריתי אתו,' 17:20) and the law's ('I will turn to you and make you fruitful,' Lev 26:9). Abraham's own fruitful-promise is written lean; Ishmael's and the covenant-law's are written full — the split exactly as the Masorah counts.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:7 (the Hilleli; the Ramah)
claim_en: THE ESTABLISH-VERB LAW, lean side: והקמתי ('and I will ESTABLISH My covenant') — doubly defective (no yod, no vav) at ALL its Torah stations: Noah's two (6:18, 9:11), this chapter's two (17:7, 17:19), Isaac's (26:3). SNAPSHOT: five, all lean.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:7 (the Ramah: 'except one')
claim_en: THE ESTABLISH-VERB LAW, full side: 'all doubly defective except ONE — והקימתי with yod' (the Bechukotai promise, Lev 26:9). SNAPSHOT: the single plene establish-token stands exactly there — the same verse that carries the fruitful-verb's plene twin: Lev 26:9 is where BOTH covenant-verbs fill out.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:8 (the Ramah: 'and every megurekha in the Torah likewise')
claim_en: מגריך ('your SOJOURNINGS' — the land promised as achuzat olam): no vav, with yod — at both Torah tokens (17:8; 28:4, Jacob blessed with 'the land of your sojournings'); the ר"ג copy's plene form appears nowhere. SNAPSHOT with the Ramah.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:20 (the Ramah — against an old tikkun's 'precise books defective')
claim_en: והרביתי ('and I will MULTIPLY him') — an old scroll-tikkun claims the precise books write it defective; the Ramah rules PLENE 'and all the Torah likewise.' SNAPSHOT: plene at all five Torah tokens (17:20, 26:4, 26:24, Exod 7:3, Lev 26:9), the defective form nowhere — the codex sides with the Ramah.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:20 (with Rabbeinu Bachye)
claim_en: שנים עשר נשיאם ('TWELVE PRINCES shall he beget') — the princes-word written WITHOUT its last yod (Minchat Shai, pointing to Rabbeinu Bachye's comment on the withheld letter). SNAPSHOT: the lean spelling exactly.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:13 (the Masorah he proves at Vayishlach; the Ramah)
claim_en: המול ימול ('he must surely be CIRCUMCISED') — the infinitive written PLENE with vav (an old tikkun floats the defective for the midrash's sake; the Masorah proves plene, the Ramah concurs). SNAPSHOT: the vav stands.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:17 (Or Torah — against the Mikra Gedolah's list)
claim_en: ויצחק ('and he LAUGHED' — the face-down laugh that will name Isaac): the chet in QAMATZ under the etnachta (the major rest) — the Mikra Gedolah's note listing it among twelve patach-at-etnachta cases is 'an error; it is not among them' (Or Torah). SNAPSHOT: qamatz on the rest, exactly.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:17 (some manuscripts; Or Torah: all Sephardic books)
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION — ha-le-ven MEAH SHANAH ('shall a HUNDRED-YEAR-old be born to?'): some manuscripts and all Sephardic books put the accent on the aleph with NO maqqef between the words; SNAPSHOT (Leningrad line) JOINS מאה to שנה with maqqef. Fourth accent-writing convention split of the run; filed, not merged.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 17:4
claim_en: אב המון ('father of a multitude') — the phrase stands TWICE in the parasha (17:4 with the lamed prefix, 17:5 bare), and the Kitzur counts the doubling itself: two av-hamon = 208 by letter-value = יצחק ('Isaac' — arithmetic named-only; the TWO-ness is the checked claim). Row 1: the bare pair at 17:5.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 17:4
claim_en: Row 2 of the doubled phrase: לאב המון ('to be a FATHER of a multitude,' 17:4) — the prefixed twin. Together with 17:5's bare pair: the parasha's exactly-two, as the Kitzur counts.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 17:14
claim_en: הפר ('he has BROKEN') — the annul-lemma's consonantal form runs four Torah tokens: the two PERFECT-pointed ('he HAS broken': the circumcision-breaker 17:14, the commandment-breaker Num 15:31 — the Masorah's pair, and the midrash reads them together: the foreskin-drawer breaks both; named) plus the vow-law's two infinitive-pointed twins (Num 30:13/16, 'her husband has annulled'). The bull-words spelled alike ride a different lemma — census lemma-locked.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:23
claim_en: וימל ('and he CIRCUMCISED') — 'the geresh (single-stroke accent) must sit on the YOD, for the word is mil-el (stress retracted).' SNAPSHOT: the stroke on the yod — the deed-verb of the selfsame day, stressed early.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:27
claim_en: ומקנת כסף ('and those BOUGHT with silver') — with maqqef, and the mem without the lengthening stroke. SNAPSHOT: joined exactly.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:27
claim_en: נמלו ('they WERE CIRCUMCISED') — the mem carries dagesh (the doubling dot). SNAPSHOT: dotted — the chapter's closing verb doubled in its middle letter.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 17:19 (the Mikra Gedolah's own correction-note)
claim_en: לזרעו אחריו ('for his seed after him' — Isaac's everlasting covenant): with LAMED alone, not the vav-prefixed form some books err into. SNAPSHOT: the bare lamed — the brit-olam clause the machine holds as FACT reads exactly as ruled.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 46:7; Shabbat 105a:2
claim_en: OUR 17:5 IS THE PROOF-SEAT OF THE ACRONYM RULE ITSELF. Asked from where in the Torah acronyms are derived, the tradition answers with THIS verse: אַב הֲמוֹן (av hamon, 'father of a multitude') read as the letters of the new name, the remaining letter carried as a remnant. At its halakhic seat, inside the Sabbath writing law, the same verse licenses the rule with a six-word expansion of the name. One of the thirty-two narrative inference rules is chartered on this unit's own verse - the interpretive method deriving its warrant from the very text this unit encodes.

check.note: This verse serving as the corpus's own charter for the acronym inference rule - the method licensed by the text the unit models.

source: Berakhot 13a:8; Bereshit Rabbah 46:8; Tosefta Berakhot 1:15; Berakhot 13a:10
claim_en: THE RENAME OF OUR 17:5 IS ENFORCED AS LAW, AND THE ENFORCEMENT IS ITSELF DISPUTED. Bar Kappara holds that whoever calls him by the former name transgresses a positive commandment; R. Eliezer holds a negative one. The objection is raised that Scripture itself later uses the old name, and answered - 'You chose him WHILE still Abram'. But the Tosefta records a COUNTER-RULE softening the whole thing: where Scripture reverts to the old name 'IT IS PRAISE, NOT SHAME; he is the same man before and after'. The parallel rename of Sarah is held to bind more narrowly, having been addressed to Abraham alone. A name-change operator in this unit generating a live, enforced and contested naming law.

check.note: A rename operator generating an enforced naming prohibition, with a recorded counter-rule at another seat and a differential scope for the parallel rename.

source: Shabbat 132a:6; Shabbat 132a:8; Shabbat 132a:10
claim_en: THE TRADITION WEIGHS THREE VERBAL ANALOGIES OVER THIS UNIT'S TOKENS AND RECORDS ITS OWN SELECTION. To establish that circumcision overrides the Sabbath, three candidate analogies are raised in turn from our chapter's words: the SIGN of 17:11 against the Sabbath's sign; the COVENANT of 17:11 against the Sabbath's covenant; and the GENERATIONS of 17:7 against the Sabbath's generations. The first two are weighed and set aside; the third survives and carries the ruling. The corpus preserves not only the conclusion but the process by which one inference was chosen over two others - the discarded candidates named.

check.note: Three candidate applications of one middah (I2) raised over this unit's tokens, two rejected and one adopted, with the rejected candidates preserved on the record.

source: Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 19:2:2; Avodah Zarah 27a:6; Bereshit Rabbah 46:12
claim_en: THE DOUBLED VERB OF OUR 17:13 IS THE BATTLEGROUND OF THE TWO GRAMMAR SCHOOLS. R. Akiva holds that doubled expressions are INCLUSIONS, and reads this doubling as adding the uncovering and the shreds to the act; R. Yishmael holds that THE TORAH SPEAKS IN ITS OWN IDIOM, doubles being mere style. The foundational dispute over how the corpus's own repetitions are to be read is fought on this unit's token. On the same doubling a further legal split rides: whether intent is required of the circumciser, one seat reading the doubled form as licensing anyone.

check.note: The two schools' foundational dispute about how doubled expressions are read, conducted on this unit's own token, with a live legal consequence.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 46:4
claim_en: ABRAHAM IS SHOWN PERFORMING A VERBAL ANALOGY, AND THE TRADITION OBJECTS THAT HE COULD NOT HAVE. The chain has him derive the site of the act by equating the covering-word used of a tree with the same word used of a man - a formal inference. R. Chanina bar Pazi objects outright: 'were the verbal analogies transmitted to Abraham?!' The answer given is that a HINT was given him in the wording. The corpus thus records a challenge to whether its own inference rules were available to the character using them, and answers it rather than suppressing it.

check.note: A character shown using a formal inference rule, with a recorded objection that the rule did not yet exist for him, and the answer preserved.

source: Kiddushin 29a:11; Avodah Zarah 26b:12; Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:7:2
claim_en: A THREE-TIER ENFORCEMENT CASCADE IS BUILT FROM THIS CHAPTER'S VERSES. The duty falls first on the father; if he fails, on THE COURT, from our 17:10's 'circumcise for yourselves every male'; and if the court fails, on the man HIMSELF, from our 17:14 with its excision penalty. Three verses of one unit supply three successive obligated parties. Eligibility is separately fixed from 17:9's 'and YOU shall keep My covenant', from which a gentile's performance is ruled invalid, and the father's duties list is anchored to 17:11 for the self-obligation case.

check.note: Three verses of one unit read as an escalating chain of obligated parties, with an eligibility rule fixed from a fourth.

source: Shabbat 132a:15; Shabbat 132a:20; Sifra, Tazria Parashat Yoledet, Chapter 1 2
claim_en: ONE CLAUSE OF OUR 17:12 DOES DOUBLE DUTY IN LAW. From 'at eight DAYS old' R. Yochanan derives that the act is performed by day and not by night; from the same clause it is derived that it is the eighth and not the seventh. And the clause closes a derivation dispute elsewhere outright, a disciple's elaborate argument dismissed with 'you dived into mighty waters and brought up a SHARD - is it not already written, at eight days?'. One numeric operator answering three separate questions.

check.note: A single numeric clause supplying three distinct legal determinations, one of them by simply closing another argument.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 46:9
claim_en: THE LAND GRANT OF OUR 17:8 IS READ AS CONDITIONED ON THE COVENANT OF OUR 17:9. R. Yudan reads five conditionals binding Godhood, the land, circumcision and the Sabbath to one another, and the sequence of these two adjacent verses is read as making the grant contingent rather than absolute - the point pressed in Joshua's speech, 'you think you enter the land uncircumcised?'. Two adjacent operators of this unit are thereby linked as condition and consequent, where the machine records them only as consecutive.

check.note: Two adjacent operators read as condition and consequent, converting an unconditional-looking grant into a contingent one.

source: Yevamot 42a:6; Yevamot 100b:9; Yevamot 64a:2
claim_en: THREE FAMILY LAWS STAND ON THE SINGLE CLAUSE OF OUR 17:7. Shmuel derives the three-month waiting period before remarriage from 'to be God to you and to your seed AFTER YOU' - read as requiring that the seed of the first be distinguishable from the seed of the second. Rav Pappa derives from the same clause the warning against marrying outside the covenant, lest the seed follow the mother. And the childless theology is read from it - where the seed is after you the Presence rests, and where not, 'on whom? on wood and stones?'. One promise clause carrying a waiting period, a marriage restriction and a theology of descent.

check.note: Three distinct family-law rules derived from a single clause of one verse.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 48:17; Rosh Hashanah 16b:6
claim_en: OUR 17:17 CARRIES A TRANSLATION ALTERATION, AND OUR 17:15-16 GROUND A REMEDY. The laughter clause is recorded as one of the places altered when the Torah was rendered for the king, the inward word rendered 'among her relatives' - so this unit joins the corpus's documented alteration census alongside Genesis 1 and 11. And R. Yitzchak lists four things that tear up a sentence - charity, crying out, CHANGE OF NAME and change of deeds - taking our 17:15-16 as the proof of the name-leg: 'Sarai shall become Sarah... and I will bless her AND GIVE YOU A SON'.

check.note: A verse enrolled in the documented translation-alteration census, and an adjacent rename supplying the proof of a named remedy in the law of decrees.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 47:6; Mekhilta DeRabbi Shimon Ben Yochai, Additions 6:2; Mishnah Nedarim 3:11
claim_en: THE DEPARTURE OF OUR 17:22 CARRIES AN ONTOLOGICAL CLAIM AND A RULE OF MANNERS. From 'God ASCENDED from upon Abraham' the leave-taking rule is derived - He took leave of him - and Reish Lakish reads the same verse as establishing that THE PATRIARCHS ARE THE CHARIOT, a claim about what these entities are, carried at a second seat inside a grading of prophecy: no thunder, no conditions, a quiet voice, the explicit name not needed. The Mishnah separately rules on our 17:1 that a man is 'not called WHOLE until he circumcised', closing with the claim that the world was not created but for this.

check.note: A departure operator grounding both a rule of manners and a claim about the ontological status of this unit's own entities.

source: Mishnah Nedarim 3:11
claim_en: THIRTEEN COVENANTS ARE CUT OVER CIRCUMCISION - AND THE COUNT IS THE CHAPTER'S OWN TOKEN CENSUS. R. Yishmael: 'great is circumcision, for thirteen covenants were cut over it.' Machine-verified against this unit's ink: the covenant-word berit stands EXACTLY THIRTEEN times in Genesis 17 - vv. 2, 4, 7 (twice), 9, 10, 11, 13 (twice), 14, 19 (twice), 21. A numeric ink claim of the never-credited-unopened class, opened and verified at the Genesis sweep (finding F-009, owner: 'Yes update'); the Step 9 engine computes it live from Data/Gen.xml.

check.note: Count berit-skeleton tokens in Gen 17: expect exactly 13. Verified 2026-08-31.

source: Sanhedrin 59b:9; Sanhedrin 59b:10; Sanhedrin 59b:11; Sanhedrin 59b:12
claim_en: THE COMMAND'S LINE-SCOPE IS DRAWN BY ITS OWN CLAUSES, IN AND OUT. The restriction: אתה וזרעך ('YOU and your seed after you,' 17:9) — Abraham's line and no one else, the sugya's answer to why the nations are unbound though the command predates Sinai; narrowed by the partitive at Gen 21:12 (IN Isaac — excluding Ishmael's sons; not ALL Isaac — excluding Esau's; G37-25's reading doing sugya work). The inclusion: את בריתי הפר ('My covenant he has BROKEN,' 17:14) — R. Yose bar Avin brings the sons of KETURAH under the duty. Seated from the Noahide exam (finding F-015, the two circumcision-scope legs).

check.note: Scope-in and scope-out of one command fixed from two clauses of this unit.

claim_en: THE CIRCUMCISION MACHINE'S FRESH LAYER, beside the unit's standing G33-21/24/25 seats. The adult's covenant-token override challenge refused on the karet distinction; leprosy overridden by the flesh-token even with a bright spot, the in-between case derived from-between-them (Abaye's common side); the site fixed by the foreskin-foreskin analogy to the fruit-making place with R. Natan's no-analogy route beside it; the agent scope at every-male-among-you; the overconfident dusk circumciser whose unfinished cut is a wound under excision; the suction safety clause; the mother exempt by him-and-not-her at Gen 21:4 with the immediate-and-for-generations rider; and the drawn foreskin re-circumcised even a hundred times by the doubled verb, the covenant-broke clause including the mashukh against R. Yehuda's answered danger arm. Filed F-117, auto-seated (round 31, the circumcision block).
